meaning: to argue a position you may not agree with, in order to test an idea
literal_translation: defender uma posição contrária apenas para testar a força de um argumento
example: In the debate, she played devil's advocate to see whether our essay could answer the strongest objection.
origin: Comes from the Catholic Church, where an official argued against a candidate's sainthood to test the case

wrong_meanings.meaning: to pretend to be a villain in a story
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom refers to arguing a position in debate, not to acting a character in fiction.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to take part in any discussion
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom means taking part actively by arguing the opposite view, not avoiding discussion.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to accept a claim without questioning it
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which means questioning a claim on purpose.

explanation: 'Play devil's advocate' means to take the opposing side of an argument on purpose, so that the group can test whether its ideas hold up. It is useful in argumentative essays and debates.
